Research & validation

Strategy Lab

Run a reproducible, cost-aware backtest from timestamped bars for one exact futures expiry and explicit candle-close signals. The engine does not fabricate ICT signals or publish strategy rankings.

P7 · REPRODUCIBLE RESEARCH

Test the rule set, not the story.

Upload one exact-expiry futures OHLC CSV with LONG / SHORT / FLAT signals. Signals are evaluated at the source-bar close and entries occur at the next bar open. Commission, slippage, risk sizing, conservative stop handling and chronological holdout testing are explicit run inputs.

USER-SUPPLIED DATA REQUIREDNo preloaded strategy performanceExisting ICT model pages are descriptions, not executable rule engines. No win rate, expectancy or model ranking is invented.

01 · Dataset & model tag

Use one exact listed contract and expiry date per run. The uploaded file stays in this browser; only its hash, manifest and completed trade ledger can sync to your private account.

No file selected. Minimum 30 timestamped bars; maximum 250,000 bars / 50 MB.
Required columns: timestamp, open, high, low, close, signal, contract, expiry. Timestamps need Z or an explicit UTC offset; expiry uses YYYY-MM-DD.

Download CSV header template →

The research tag is only a label. None of the ten listed ICT candidates has a machine-testable detector here. See the rule-card status and decisions required.

02 · Execution & costs

Tick size/value must match this exact contract and currency. Verify current exchange specifications and enter all per-side broker, exchange, clearing, NFA and routing fees.

Costs are applied per contract. Entry and stop/time-exit slippage are embedded in fill prices; commission is charged on both sides. A limit target is filled at its target price without queue or partial-fill simulation. Position size rounds down to whole contracts. Spread is not separately modeled; account for it conservatively in slippage or do not treat this as execution evidence.

03 · Chronological holdout

The data is split by time, not randomly. Each period starts flat with independent starting capital; no position is carried across period boundaries.

Out-of-sample = remainder. Keep this final segment untouched until rules and parameters are frozen. The tool does not optimize settings; inspecting OOS and then changing rules turns it into another in-sample period.
Choose a valid CSV to enable the engine.

Runs stay local unless you sign in. Signed-in runs and trade ledgers sync to your user-owned Supabase tables.

04 · Method contract

  • Signal is known only at its source candle close; entry is next-bar open.
  • One position at a time; no pyramiding; no simultaneous reverse entry.
  • If stop and target are both touched in one bar, stop is assumed first.
  • Gaps through stops fill at the worse opening price plus configured slippage.
  • Expectancy and net profit factor use P&L after modeled costs.
  • Fixed-interval timestamp gaps are reported; the engine cannot distinguish session closures from missing bars.
  • ICT model choices are research labels; signals are externally supplied and their causality is not audited.
  • No automatic event/news filter, exchange session/expiry calendar, separate spread, or roll handling is configured.
  • Drawdown uses bar-close mark-to-market equity with estimated exit costs reserved.
  • Historical roll fills, margin, liquidity, market impact and broker-specific execution are not inferred.

Evidence rules

Win rate alone is not a decision metric. Review trade count, net expectancy, average R, net profit factor, drawdown size/duration, costs and out-of-sample stability together. Small samples, externally generated signals with look-ahead, unadjusted contract rolls, inaccurate tick values and omitted costs can invalidate results. A backtest is not a forecast or a guarantee of future performance.
